body: Fear Effect 2: Retro Helix is Kronos Digital Entertainment's PlayStation action-adventure, first released in North America on 21 February 2001. Set in 2048, it precedes the original game and follows the circumstances that bring Hana, Glas and Deke together with Rain Qin. A degenerative pandemic has reshaped their world, where freelance operations and personal motives lead the characters into a larger conspiracy. The prequel expands the relationships behind the original cast while retaining its mixture of cinematic scenes, action and puzzles. Familiar faces enter the story from different starting points.

The journey moves from a futuristic Hong Kong to Xi'an, the tomb of China's first emperor and the mythical island of Penglai Shan. Each location gives the investigation another visual and narrative setting, connecting espionage to the series' supernatural interests. The player switches between characters as events bring their motives into contact. Exploration and puzzle solving interrupt the action, asking for attention to the situation instead of treating every scene as a fight. The campaign gradually turns separate operations into a shared problem whose scale extends beyond the mercenaries' original intentions.

Stanley Liu directed and wrote the prequel, with David Rovin composing the music. Its illustrated characters and cinematic environments continue the original game's recognisable presentation, making the connection between the two adventures visible even as the chronology moves backwards. Rain's arrival gives Hana another important relationship and enlarges the group's history. Released during the PlayStation's later years, Retro Helix uses a sequel's opportunity to deepen an existing cast. Its central question is how people with incompatible backgrounds and immediate goals come to take part in the same dangerous undertaking.
story_headings: Before the mercenaries became a team
Follow a conspiracy through changing places
The same visual language, another history
